note: Explicit, reviewed errata applied on top of the vendored upstream colors.json by scripts/palette-sources/wada1.mjs. The upstream file is never edited. Every `from` value below is asserted against the vendored file before `to` is applied, so this patch fails loudly if the pinned source is ever changed.
hexPolicy: The four CMYK fixes below are NOT reflected in `hex`. Upstream hex is produced by an ICC transform (U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2 -> sRGB IEC61966-2.1, relative colorimetric + black point compensation) that this repo cannot run: the Adobe ICC profile is not redistributable and the pipeline would be a new dependency. Until someone recomputes these four through that same transform, we keep mattdesl's existing hex, which is visually close (the CMYK deltas are small K shifts) and is what every other published dataset shows. Corrected CMYK is carried in the data so the recompute is a one-line change later.

cmyk.name: Citrine
cmyk.why: Book has K=7; reported by the book owner in issue #1 and matched independently by the vol. 2 transcription.

cmyk.name: Rainette Green
cmyk.why: Book has K=28; same two independent confirmations.

cmyk.name: Diamine Green
cmyk.why: Book has 87/20/100/10; same two independent confirmations.

cmyk.name: Dull Violet Black
cmyk.why: M=106 is impossible (CMYK is 0-100); the book reads 100/90/38/50. This is the only upstream value that is invalid rather than merely wrong.

namesWhy.typos: The first nine are transcription typos in the upstream file; the book spellings are the ones in issue #1 and open PR #2.
namesWhy.duplicates: Eugenia Red and Grayish Lavender are two distinct colours each, sharing one book name. Upstream disambiguates them with two different ad-hoc separators; we only normalise the separator to '(A)' / '(B)' and keep both entries. The suffix is ours, not the book's.

notApplied.marcebollin: marcebollin/sanzo-wada-colors additionally changes Red Y 70->90, Pinkish Cinnamon C 5->0, Cinnamon Buff M 25->23 and Olive C 48->18. The issue #1 reporter (who owns the book) found only the four discrepancies above, and the independent vol. 2 book transcription keeps mattdesl's values for all four, so these are treated as transcription errors and are not applied.
